title: Flaky eval detection + quarantine workflow for Optimize quality gates
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context / problem
Optimize quality gates rely on offline eval prompt sets. During beta we’ve seen intermittent failures (same config diff, different outcomes) driven by:
- Non-determinism in model/runtime execution (quant kernels, scheduling) + stochastic decoding settings
- Noisy rubrics / borderline prompts that flip pass/fail
- Regional capacity variance (EU-West timeouts / throttling) causing partial runs
- Prompt set drift / accidental modifications of “goldens”

Today the gating state machine treats these as “fail”, which blocks cost-saving changes and drives manual escalations. We need a first-class flakiness signal, rerun/aggregation policy, and the ability to quarantine known-flaky prompt sets so they don’t page/oncall or block rollouts.

Goals
1) Detect flaky suites/prompt sets and produce a stable flake signal (suite-level + prompt-set level) that can be used in the gate decision.
2) Provide quarantine workflow (admin-only) to temporarily exclude flaky prompt sets from gating decisions, with strict auditability.
3) Provide rerun tooling + attribution so we can answer: “Was this a real regression or just variance?” and “Where did variance come from (region, GPU SKU, seed, runtime version)?”
4) Avoid alert storms and reduce false-positive gate failures while maintaining rigor.

Non-goals (MVP)
- Rewriting the entire eval harness scoring system.
- Full private/on-prem automation (manual/quarantine documented workflow is OK).

Proposed approach (implementation plan)
A) Flake scoring + rerun/aggregation policy (eval-harness)
- Implement/standardize a flake_score for each suite and prompt set:
  - Run-level: record per-prompt outcomes + rubric score distributions
  - Aggregate across N runs (default N=3 for suspected flake, N=2 for normal retries)
  - Compute: failure_rate, stddev, and a normalized flake_score (0–1) using Sana/Selene’s variance guidance.
- Rerun policy:
  - If initial run fails and delta is within “borderline band” (see thresholds doc), auto-rerun up to max_reruns=2.
  - If failures are inconsistent across reruns, mark result as FLAKY rather than FAILED.
  - If consistent regression across reruns, mark as FAILED.
- Persist artifacts for each rerun and final aggregation:
  - prompt_set_id, suite_id, gate_run_id
  - seed, decoding params snapshot, runtime version, model version, region, GPU sku
  - per-metric deltas + confidence intervals

B) Quarantine workflow (Optimize + admin tooling)
- Add quarantine flags to prompt sets at gating time:
  - quarantine_status: active | expired | none
  - reason_code: flaky_rubric | nondeterministic_model | infra_noise | timeout_hotspot | other
  - owner (who quarantined), expires_at, ticket_link (required)
- Enforcement:
  - If a prompt set is quarantined, it is excluded from gate pass/fail computation BUT still runs optionally for monitoring (configurable).
  - Gate result must clearly show “excluded due to quarantine” and should reduce confidence score.
  - If quarantine reduces coverage below minimum coverage thresholds, gate should return “INCONCLUSIVE” and block apply unless override is granted.

C) Attribution + observability (metrics + drilldowns)
- Emit metrics/tags for:
  - gate_run.flake_detected (boolean)
  - gate_run.rerun_count
  - prompt_set.quarantined (boolean) + reason_code
  - suite.failure_inconsistency_rate
  - eval_run.env tags: region, gpu_sku, runtime_version, model_family
- Console visibility (minimal for MVP; full UI is ENG-3925):
  - Gate run summary includes: “Flaky detected” badge, rerun count, link to aggregated artifact bundle.
  - Provide API fields so Console can show: quarantined prompt sets + who/when/why.

User stories
1) As oncall (SRE/ML), when a gate fails, I can see whether it was consistent across reruns, and if not, I can treat it as flaky and avoid rollback thrash.
2) As Evals lead, I can quarantine a prompt set that is causing noisy failures, with an expiration, and the system will stop using it for pass/fail until fixed.
3) As runtime engineer, I can identify whether variance correlates with a GPU SKU, runtime version, or region.

Acceptance criteria
- Gate runs can end in one of: PASSED, FAILED, FLAKY, INCONCLUSIVE (in addition to existing states), with deterministic rules and explicit reasons.
- Automatic reruns happen only in well-defined cases (borderline band, timeouts) and are bounded.
- Flake signal is stored and queryable per suite and per prompt set (last_7d, last_30d).
- Quarantine actions are admin-only, require: reason_code, expires_at, and ticket_link; changes are audit logged.
- Quarantined prompt sets are excluded from pass/fail aggregation, and this exclusion is visible in the gate result payload.
- Metrics exist to alert on:
  - flake_rate spikes
  - quarantine_count spikes
  - high rerun_count leading to latency SLO risk

- Eval-harness integration contract — sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/gating-integration-contracts.json
- Related PR (eval-harness): PR-418 “add flake score and rerun policy” — sources/github/eval-harness/pr-418-add-flake-score-and-rerun-policy.json
- Related incidents/support:
  - SUP-18421 false positive block (flake) — sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-18421-optimize-change-blocked-by-quality-gate-false-positive.json
  - SUP-18487 timeouts EU-West — sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-18487-quality-gate-run-timeouts-in-eu-west.json

Open questions
- What is the default behavior for FLAKY at apply-time?
  - Proposal: treat as “block by default” for auto-apply; allow one-click apply only with explicit override + shorter TTL.
- Do we quarantine at prompt_set_id only, or also at suite_id?
  - Proposal: both, but MVP is prompt_set_id; suite-level quarantine is a follow-on.
- Where should quarantine metadata live?
  - Proposal: in Optimize gating DB (source of truth) with periodic sync from eval-harness prompt registry.

Work breakdown
ENG-3929-A (eval-harness): implement rerun policy + aggregation artifacts + flake_score
ENG-3929-B (Optimize service): store flake metadata on gate_run; add new terminal states; expose via API
ENG-3929-C (admin tooling): quarantine create/list/expire endpoints + audit events + metric emissions

Risks
- Over-rerunning increases gate latency and cost. Mitigation: strict rerun cap + only rerun borderline.
- Quarantine could mask real regressions. Mitigation: quarantines expire, require ticket, reduce confidence, enforce min coverage.
- Region-specific infra noise may look like flake. Mitigation: attribute timeouts separately; tag infra-related failures.

Progress updates
- 2026-01-08 (Olivia Grant): Drafted state mapping for PASSED/FAILED/FLAKY/INCONCLUSIVE; aligned with Selene Huang on borderline rerun criteria. Waiting on final threshold bands from Applied ML.
- 2026-01-19 (Sahana Iyer): Noted GPU scarcity impact on reruns in CI; recommend rerun jobs be queued with lower priority and be cancellable.
- 2026-01-27 (Allison Grant): Observability ask: flake_rate must be separated from fail_rate in dashboards to avoid noisy pages.
- 2026-02-05 (Olivia Grant): Eval-harness PR-418 merged; starting Optimize-side wiring + persistence. Next: quarantine endpoints + audit events.
- 2026-02-16 (Sean Gallagher): Requested default page suppression: do not page oncall for FLAKY unless flake_rate crosses threshold for >30m.
- 2026-02-22 (Olivia Grant): Implemented data model draft for quarantine (prompt_set_id, expires_at, owner, reason_code, ticket_link). Need review from Marcus Lin on admin/RBAC boundaries.

Notes for QA
- Test matrix should include:
  - deterministic fail (should remain FAILED across reruns)
  - borderline variance (should become FLAKY with rerun_count>0)
  - infra timeouts partial run (should rerun; if persists, mark INCONCLUSIVE with reason=infra_timeout)
  - quarantine active reduces coverage below min -> INCONCLUSIVE
  - quarantine active but coverage still sufficient -> decision computed and includes exclusion list
